findings.title: parseBody() breaks after c.req.formData() was already called
findings.why_it_matters: A handler that calls `c.req.parseBody()` after anything earlier in the chain called `c.req.formData()` now fails: multipart requests throw `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData` (HTTP 500), and urlencoded requests silently return one garbage key holding the raw multipart text instead of the fields. Both worked at the base, where parseBody returned the cached FormData. The cause is that parseBody now always asks for `arrayBuffer()`; with only `formData` cached, HonoRequest rebuilds the bytes via `new Response(formData)`, which re-serializes as multipart with a fresh boundary, and those bytes are then parsed against the original Content-Type. Reusing `bodyCache.formData` when present, as validator.ts:115-116 already does, restores the old behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData, short-circuit on an existing cache before reading bytes, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `let formData: FormData; if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer(); const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || ''); if (request instanceof HonoRequest) { request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise as unknown as FormData } formData = await formDataPromise }`. Add tests in src/request.test.ts for `await req.formData()` followed by `await req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

src/request.ts:228-235 -- const anyCachedKey = Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]; if (anyCachedKey) { return (bodyCache[anyCachedKey]).then((body) => { ... return new Response(body)[key]() }) }  (with only `formData` cached, arrayBuffer() is new Response(formData).arrayBuffer(): a multipart re-serialization with a newly generated boundary)
base 97287029 src/utils/body.ts -- const formData = await (request as Request).formData()  (returned the cached FormData via request.ts:222-226)

Empirical run (scratch bundle of head vs base source, Node 24.21.0). HonoRequest multipart, `await req.formData(); await req.parseBody()`: head => THROW TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData (cause: no boundary found in multipart body); base => {foo:'bar', n:'1'}.

Empirical run, urlencoded body 'foo=bar&n=1', same call order: head => {"------formdata-undici-045754882727
Content-Disposition: form-data; name": ""foo"

bar
..."}; base => {foo:'bar', n:'1'}.

Empirical run through Hono app (middleware `await c.req.formData()`, handler `c.json(await c.req.parseBody())`): head multipart => status 500 'Internal Server Error', head urlencoded => 200 with the garbage key; base => 200 {"foo":"bar"} for both.
src/validator/validator.ts:115-116 -- if (c.req.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await c.req.bodyCache.formData }  (existing cache-first pattern the fix should mirror)

residual_risks: Behavior was verified only on Node 24 (undici). parseBody no longer calls the runtime's native request.formData(); it reads arrayBuffer() and parses through new Response(...).formData(). Bun, Deno, Workers and Lambda runtime tests were not run (forbidden by the execution policy), so parity of that path on those runtimes is unconfirmed.
testing_gaps: No test covers the new cache write at src/utils/body.ts:130: parseBody() followed by c.req.formData() / c.req.text() / cloneRawRequest() on the same HonoRequest for a form body. A scratch run shows these work at head (cache keys become [arrayBuffer, formData]; text() now returns the original bytes), but nothing pins it.
